chapter: Leaving Duke and the Goodman sextet
title: How Benny Goodman hired him
summary: Goodman approached Cootie through his brother Irving; he liked the band's beat, and the pay was settled in New York.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Okay, Cootie, now we get to -- we're up to 1940 here, and we started talking about Duke when Benny got in touch with you. So I'm interested in all this. First of all, do you remember how Benny got in touch with you? Who did he go through?
Oh, I think he went through his brother.
No, not Freddie. The other one.
He got Irving to approach you, huh?
Yeah. Irving. But I liked the band. that was the main thing. (Unintelligible) A The band had a terrific beat.
Well, when did you hear the band? On records?
The band had a terrific beat.
Oh, Gene Krupa was on drums, and --
I think -- yeah, Davey Tough was.
Well, Davey was a very good drummer, wasn't he?
Davey Tough. Yeah. He had a terrific
And I just liked the band.
I liked the sound of the band.
Yeah. And you liked what Goodman was laying down, didn't you?
I liked -- I liked -- he could play, you know. And that's the reason why.
Yeah. Because, that's -- I mean, that band was jumping, wasn't it? And --
I mean, they came on the scene with something that was something else, wasn't it?
Well, that was -- so, when you joined the band, I think they were in New York, weren't they?

So what -- well, you were now -- well, we needn't pull any punches on this. We know -- I mean, I know Benny well, so Benny wasn't -- it started off he didn't want to offer you too much money to start with, I'm sure.
Yeah, what to tell him. No, that wasn't enough.
So he got to figuring what he thought it was okay, and he said, "Well, tell him okay."
